lane: datum-offset — Lake Lahontan shoreline datum as a strain gauge
candidate: historical v8 artifact; no new candidate was emitted after the strict duplicate stop
hypothesis: Fault displacement after the Lake Lahontan highstand produces a step or lateral deflection in a smooth, rebound-corrected shoreline datum; a fault trace cuts across datum contours, unlike many constructional shoreline features.
mechanism: Flat-pixel shoreline benches in the 25 m USGS 3DEP DEM; robust quadratic isobase; Frangi ridge of the elevation residual; cross-datum step gate; DEM-ridge trace extension; dotted emission.
named_non_fault_mimic: Wave-cut bluffs, beach berms, fan-head risers, delta topsets, and spatially variable isostatic rebound can create apparent shoreline steps or deflections without a fault.

holdout.ci_method: Percentile bootstrap resampling the six spatial folds as clusters; 10,000 replicates, seed 62. Coarse six-cluster uncertainty.
holdout.protocol: Six spatial folds (3 by 2); 3 px erosion; visible-catalogue truth in each eroded block; pooled distance-weighted Tversky DTI, alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, 300 m triangular kernel.
holdout.interpretation: Catalogue-based proxy only. It cannot validate faults absent from the catalogue, is not an organizer score, and does not authorize a submission slot.

leakage_canary.verdict: no canary alarm; AUCs are near chance, indicating little catalogue-prediction signal, not proving absence of every leakage mode
